preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1]) and all(2 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 100 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1])
preconditions.description: The first line contains two integers n and k where 2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5 and 2 ≤ k ≤ 100.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == 2 and all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**5 for x in stdin.splitlines()[1].split())
preconditions.description: The second line contains exactly n integers a₁, ..., aₙ where each 1 ≤ aᵢ ≤ 10^5.
The number of integers in the second line matches n.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the count of valid pairs.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= i < j <= n for i, j in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[1].split()[i_idx]), int(stdin.splitlines()[1].split()[j_idx])) for i_idx, j_idx in [(i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n)] if (int(stdin.splitlines()[1].split()[i_idx]) * int(stdin.splitlines()[1].split()[j_idx])) in {x**k for x in range(1, int(max(stdin.splitlines()[1].split())) + 1)}])
postconditions.description: For every pair (i, j) where 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n, the product aᵢ * aⱼ equals xᵏ for some integer x, if and only if the pair is counted in the output.
